rubrics.criterion: The stored-value size policy mechanics — how a value's size is measured, how that measurement is compared against the configured limit, and how a violation is enforced — are implemented in one shared owner that the participating drivers' write paths call, and no participating driver keeps its own private inline copy of that comparison-and-reaction logic.
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because every participating write path re-implements the same size guard locally; relocating the decision so it is made in exactly one place is the requested semantic outcome, while the chosen module, helper names, and signatures are left to the solution.

rubrics.criterion: Every write path in the drivers under src/drivers that previously carried its own size guard now delegates to the shared mechanism — including drivers that have two write methods, both of their guarded methods route through it, and the driver whose two write methods previously shared a private local closure use the shared mechanism in both call sites.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that consolidates only some of the guarded write paths still leaves the size policy scattered; this identifies the hidden completeness requirement without requiring a specific file inventory, since the guarded write paths are discoverable from the repository and the responsibility manifest.

rubrics.criterion: Each driver still states its own policy decision through the shared mechanism: cache-like drivers silently skip oversized writes instead of storing or throwing, committed stores throw a driver-annotated error, and the existing per-call override of the limit (transaction option taking precedence over the driver option, where it exists today) still resolves the same way.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation must not flatten the deliberate per-driver skip-vs-throw difference or the one existing per-write override; preserving these decisions is a distinct obligation from centralizing the mechanics, and losing them would be a behavior regression that the unit tests do not cover.

rubrics.criterion: The size measurement applied by the guard is defined once and applied uniformly by all participating write paths, so drivers no longer measure the same conceptual quantity differently, ending the current mixture of character counts and byte counts.
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt explicitly asks for the unit ambiguity to be brought under control with one well-defined measurement; a repair that keeps per-driver units has not completed the requested change even if the comparison logic is centralized.

rubrics.criterion: The maxItemSize option typing is declared once and reused by the participating drivers' options interfaces, so the drivers no longer each re-declare the same option field independently.
rubrics.rationale: Independent per-interface re-declaration of the option is part of the duplicated policy in this case; sharing the type is a coupled fact with consolidating the guard and separating it would leave the responsibility split across interfaces and write paths.

rubrics.criterion: Errors raised for oversized writes come from the shared mechanism and keep the existing driver-annotated error family (errors identify the refusing driver in the established format), rather than each driver composing its own ad-hoc rejection wording.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt asks that the error contract be defined once; this grades whether the failure contract is truly part of the shared owner without constraining exact message strings, since any wording is acceptable as long as it is shared and driver-attributed.

rubrics.criterion: The per-driver artifacts the consolidation replaced are deleted: the removed comparisons, their local measurement bindings or expressions, and the private shared closure are taken out of the driver files rather than left in place beside the new mechanism, and imports that only served the removed inline logic are dropped.
rubrics.rationale: Leftover dead copies of the guard next to the shared mechanism would keep the original duplication in the codebase and reintroduce exactly the drift the task is about; cleaning them up is a completion obligation distinct from adding the shared owner.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves no newly-dead code around the guarded write paths, such as an unused measurement helper or byte-size utility left behind at a call site, an unused error-factory import in a driver that no longer raises its own guard error, or an unused exported helper kept in the shared utilities area.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for this instance is a partially-applied consolidation that rewires call sites but strands the now-unreachable locals and imports from the old private copies, which reviewers of this codebase would have to clean up afterwards.

rubrics.criterion: Drivers behave exactly as before when no size limit is configured, and public creation APIs keep their current compatibility, including calling the memory driver with no options at all.
rubrics.rationale: The limit is opt-in in this case; the consolidation must not tighten default behavior or break existing factory signatures, which the baseline tests and typecheck do not fully guard for the new option.

rubrics.criterion: A refused write has no side effects beyond the refusal, exactly as before the change: no expiry timer is armed, no request is sent, nothing touches disk, and no cache entry is displaced by a value that is then rejected.
rubrics.rationale: The guards deliberately sit before store-specific work; a repair that checks the limit after starting that work, or partially performs it before failing, changes externally observable behavior that no test pins down.

rubrics.criterion: The repair keeps the stored-value size-limiting capability intact for all participating drivers rather than removing or disabling it, for example by dropping the maxItemSize option and its enforcement, hardcoding the limit, or making the shared mechanism a no-op.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting the feature would trivially eliminate the duplication; this is the instance-specific evasion of the requested semantics and must fail grading even though it makes the stray-logic check pass.

rubrics.criterion: The change does not modify behavior of the responsibilities adjacent to the guarded write paths: TTL/expiry scheduling and transaction TTL handling, the lru library's own size and entry-count options pass-through, readOnly guards, key normalization, and base-key prefix handling.
rubrics.rationale: The guarded sites sit inside write methods that also implement these neighboring behaviors, so an imprecise consolidation can easily disturb them; this failure mode is specific to the participating driver code in this instance.
